collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: About 30 calls a week get missed
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: thinks it’s an AI scam/gadget; needs proof it’s legitimate

transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Totally fair to be skeptical—most of the “AI” stuff online is hype. The simplest way to tell if Dialux is legit is this: when a new customer calls and nobody answers, what happens today—does it go to voicemail, a cell phone, or does it just get missed?
User: It usually just gets missed. But how do I know you aren't some robot collecting my info to sell?
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—nobody wants their info sold. We don’t sell your data; we only use what’s needed to see if we can stop those missed calls, and if you do a setup, everything stays tied to your business systems.  

What kind of business is this for?
User: It's roofing—Ortiz Roofing in Dallas. But how can I trust this isn't recorded and monitored by some third party?
Agent: Got it—roofing in Dallas, and privacy’s a real concern. When you say “recorded and monitored,” are you mainly worried about call audio being stored somewhere, or customer details (name/address/insurance info) being accessed?
User: Both, honestly. I don't want any of my customer details or my conversations being shared or sold.
Agent: Makes sense—if you can’t trust where the audio and customer details go, it’s a non-starter. Roughly how many new calls a week do you think you’re missing right now?
User: About 30 calls a week get missed. But how do I know this isn't just another scheme to get my data?
Agent: Yeah—missing ~30 calls a week is a lot of money walking away, so you’re right to be careful. If I can show you exactly what customer info would (and wouldn’t) be captured, stored, and who has access—would you be open to that?
User: Alright, show me this data stuff. But if it sounds fishy, I'm out immediately.
Agent: Totally fair—here’s the clean version: we only capture what’s needed to book the job (name, phone, address, issue), we don’t sell it, and access is restricted to you/your team; call recordings can be turned off, and if they’re on, they’re used strictly for quality and are not shared.  

Before I go deeper—are you mostly trying to protect customer privacy, or are you also worried about competitors getting your pricing/job details?
User: Mostly worried about customer privacy. But competitors getting job details is a concern too. How do you ensure security?
Agent: Got it—customer privacy first, and you don’t want job details leaking to competitors either. On the security side, is your bigger concern who at Dialux could access it, or the software vendors involved (like phone/CRM providers) having visibility?
User: Both, honestly. I don't want any of my customer details or my conversations being shared or sold.
Agent: Makes sense—if you can’t trust where the audio and customer details go, it’s a non-starter. Roughly how many new calls a week do you think you’re missing right now?
User: About 30 calls a week get missed. But how do I know this isn't just another scheme to get my data?
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—if it’s a data grab, you shouldn’t touch it. Of those 30 missed calls, what percent do you think would’ve actually booked if you’d answered—like 25%, 50%, 60%?
User: Probably about 40% would book. But how do I know you're not just using this to sell me something?
Agent: Got it—40%. And I get the concern: the only reason I’m asking is to see if the missed calls are worth fixing in the first place, using your numbers.  

What’s your average roofing job value—are we talking $5,000, $8,000, $12,000?
User: Average job is around $1,800. But who sees this info? I want to know who has access.
Agent: On the numbers first—if you booked even 40% of those 30 missed calls at about $1,800, that’s about **$21600 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$93500/mo** over a month. Does that sound about right?

On access: by default it’s your team, and we can restrict/role-limit it; are you asking about access for Dialux staff, or any outside vendors too?
User: Alright, those numbers are something. How do you handle staff access? No outside vendors, right?
Agent: Got it—on staff access, we can set it so only specific people on your team can see customer details (and limit what they can see), and no, we’re not sharing or selling your customer info to outside vendors.  

It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay where he’ll show you the exact access controls and what gets stored—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, later today works. But I expect full transparency during this walkthrough. How do I confirm this slot?
Agent: Absolutely—full transparency is the whole point of the 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay. Before I can lock anything in and get you the SMS confirmation, what’s your first name?
User: I'll give my first name once I'm sure this isn't a trap. What do you need it for?
Agent: Got it—I’m not trying to trap you. I need your first name purely so Jay knows who he’s meeting on the calendar and so the SMS confirmation isn’t anonymous; nothing gets sold or shared.  

What first name should I put it under?
User: Alright, it's Sam. But I expect this Jay to be clear and upfront during the call.
Agent: Got it, Sam—and yes, Jay will be direct and upfront. And your last name is Ortiz, with Ortiz Roofing, right?
User: Correct, Ortiz Roofing. But I expect no funny business with my info. This call better be straightforward.
Agent: Absolutely, Sam—straightforward and no funny business. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the SMS confirmation?
User: Yeah, +14695550001. But remember, no spam or misuse. I'm only doing this because you convinced me.
Agent: Got it—no spam, and we’ll only use it for the SMS confirmation and the walkthrough logistics. And which time zone are you in—Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Central Time. But I hope this doesn't mean you'll be calling at strange hours. Keep it reasonable.
Agent: Totally reasonable—we’ll keep it in normal business hours, Central Time. I can get you in **today at 5:30 PM** or **6:15 PM** Central— which works?
User: Let's do 6:15 PM. But I expect this call to be clear and no-nonsense, or I'm out.
Agent: Perfect—thanks, Sam. I’ve got you down for today at 6:15 PM Central with Jay; he’ll keep it clear and no-nonsense and walk through the exact access controls and what’s stored. If anything feels off, you can stop the call anytime. Talk soon—bye.
